hints: Focus on the two separate clues, Fehling's tells you the functional group while cis-trans tells you about the shape around the double bond.
Remember Fehling's gives a red-brown precipitate of Cu2O only with aldehydes, so look for which structures contain a -CHO group.
For cis-trans, check each C of the C=C separately, both carbons must have two different groups attached for isomerism to be possible.
walkthrough:
**Use Fehling's Test To Find The Functional Group**

Fehling's solution is a specific test for aldehydes. It oxidises an aldehyde and is itself reduced to red-brown copper(I) oxide.

$$\text{R-CHO + 2Cu}^{2+} + 5\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{R-COO}^- + \text{Cu}_2\text{O (red-brown)} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Eliminate The Ketone**

Ketones like $\text{-COCH}_3$ are not oxidised by Fehling's, so they give no precipitate. This immediately rules out any structure containing only a ketone group.

**Apply The Cis-Trans Rule**

For cis/trans isomerism, each carbon of the $\text{C=C}$ must be joined to two different groups. If either $\text{C}$ has two identical groups, like two $\text{H}$ atoms, cis/trans is impossible.

Check: $\text{C}$ with $\text{H}$ and $\text{H}$ = no isomerism. $\text{C}$ with $\text{H}$ and $\text{CH}_3$ = isomerism possible.

**Combine Both Clues To Identify P**

P must have an aldehyde $\text{-CHO}$ group AND have two different groups on each alkene carbon. Only the structure $\text{CH}_3\text{(H)C=C(H)(CHO)}$ satisfies both conditions at once.

options.A: Contains an aldehyde in the $\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ group so it would give Fehling's positive, but the left $\text{C=C}$ carbon has two $\text{H}$ atoms. With two identical groups on one carbon, cis/trans isomerism is impossible.
options.B: Has two different groups on each $\text{C=C}$ carbon ($\text{H}$/$\text{CH}_3$ on left, $\text{COCH}_3$/$\text{H}$ on right) so it can show cis/trans, but the $\text{COCH}_3$ group is a ketone, not an aldehyde. Ketones do not react with Fehling's solution.
options.C: Contains an aldehyde $\text{CHO}$ so it would give the red-brown precipitate, but the left $\text{C=C}$ carbon again has $\text{H}$ and $\text{H}$. This common trap tests aldehyde recognition alone, but it fails the cis/trans requirement.
options.D: Perfect match for both clues. It is an aldehyde ($\text{-CHO}$) so it reduces Fehling's to red-brown $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$. The left carbon has $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{H}$, and the right carbon has $\text{H}$ and $\text{CHO}$, so both carbons have two different groups and cis/trans isomerism is possible.
